cancel_emergency_retries.description: Stop an emergency-priority notification from being retried any further, without waiting for someone to acknowledge it. Use this when the condition that raised the alert has cleared on its own.
cancel_emergency_retries.name: cancel_emergency_retries

parameters.description: The receipt returned by Send Pushover notification when it was sent at emergency priority.
parameters.name: receipt

check_receipt.description: Check whether an emergency-priority notification has been acknowledged yet, and by whom. Poll this to hold a workflow until someone confirms they have seen an alert.
check_receipt.name: check_receipt

parameters.description: The receipt returned by Send Pushover notification when it was sent at emergency priority.
parameters.name: receipt

acknowledged.description: True once someone has acknowledged the notification, which also stops the retries.

acknowledged_at.description: When it was acknowledged, as a Unix timestamp. Null if it has not been.

acknowledged_by.description: User key of whoever acknowledged it, which is how you tell who responded in a delivery group.

acknowledged_by_device.description: Name of the device they acknowledged it on.

called_back.description: True once Pushover has POSTed to the callback URL, if one was given.

called_back_at.description: When the callback fired, as a Unix timestamp.

expired.description: True once Pushover has stopped retrying because the expire window passed without an acknowledgement.

expires_at.description: When retrying stops, as a Unix timestamp.

last_delivered_at.description: When the most recent retry went out, as a Unix timestamp.

get_app_limits.description: Check how many messages your Pushover application has left this month and when the counter resets. Useful as a guard before a workflow that sends in bulk.
get_app_limits.name: get_app_limits

limit.description: Messages the application may send per month.

remaining.description: Messages left before the limit is reached.

reset_at.description: When the counter resets, as a Unix timestamp.

list_sounds.description: List the notification sounds your Pushover application can ask for, with the name to pass as the sound of a notification and the label the Pushover apps show for it.
list_sounds.name: list_sounds

label.description: How the sound is named in the Pushover apps, e.g. Siren (long).

name.description: Value to pass as the sound of a notification, e.g. siren.

send_notification.description: Send a push notification to your phone, tablet, or desktop. Set the priority to emergency to have Pushover keep retrying until someone acknowledges it, which returns a receipt you can poll.
send_notification.name: send_notification

parameters.description: The notification body, up to 1024 characters. Supports basic HTML tags when html is turned on.
parameters.name: message

parameters.description: Heading shown above the message, up to 250 characters. Defaults to your application's name.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: Who to notify, as a Pushover user key or delivery group key. Leave blank to use the key saved with the connection.
parameters.name: user_key

parameters.description: How intrusive the notification is. Emergency repeats until acknowledged; high bypasses the user's quiet hours; lowest delivers with no alert at all.
parameters.name: priority

parameters.description: Which sound to play, e.g. pushover, siren, magic, or none for silence. Use List Pushover sounds to see them all. Defaults to the user's own setting.
parameters.name: sound

parameters.description: A link to show under the message, up to 512 characters.
parameters.name: url

parameters.description: Text to show for the link instead of the raw URL, up to 100 characters.
parameters.name: url_title

parameters.description: Send only to one of the user's devices, by its Pushover device name. Leave blank to reach all of them.
parameters.name: device

parameters.description: Render basic HTML in the message, such as <b> and <a>. Cannot be combined with monospace.
parameters.name: html

parameters.description: Render the message in a fixed-width font, useful for logs or tables. Cannot be combined with html.
parameters.name: monospace

parameters.description: Seconds after which the notification is removed from the user's devices automatically.
parameters.name: ttl

parameters.description: Emergency priority only: how many seconds between retries, at least 30. Defaults to 60.
parameters.name: retry

parameters.description: Emergency priority only: how many seconds to keep retrying before giving up, up to 10800 (3 hours). Defaults to 3600.
parameters.name: expire

parameters.description: Emergency priority only: a URL Pushover will POST to once someone acknowledges the notification.
parameters.name: callback

parameters.description: Emergency priority only: comma-separated labels you can later use to cancel a batch of notifications at once.
parameters.name: tags

receipt.description: Tracking id for an emergency-priority notification, used by Check Pushover receipt and Cancel Pushover retries. Null at every other priority.

request_id.description: Pushover's id for this request, which their support asks for when tracing a delivery.

validate_user.description: Check that a Pushover user or group key is valid and has at least one active device. Use this before sending to a key that came from somewhere else in the workflow, so a bad key fails visibly rather than silently going nowhere.
validate_user.name: validate_user

parameters.description: Who to notify, as a Pushover user key or delivery group key. Leave blank to use the key saved with the connection.
parameters.name: user_key

parameters.description: Also check that this specific device name exists on the account.
parameters.name: device

devices.description: Names of the devices registered to the key, which can be passed as the device of a notification.

is_group.description: True when the key names a delivery group rather than a single user.

licenses.description: Platforms the user is licensed for, e.g. Android, iOS, Desktop.

description: Send push notifications to your phone, tablet, or desktop with Pushover: choose a sound and priority, attach a link, raise an emergency alert that repeats until someone acknowledges it, and check your remaining monthly quota.
